model: print-in-place sauropod dinosaur, 1 fixed body + 3 tail segments, 3 Z-axis pin joints

envelope_mm.note: neutral (as printed) pose; checked also with the tail swung: all joints at +30 deg gives Y extent 49.6 mm, still < 50

print_settings_assumed.orientation: as modelled, legs and whole tail flat on the bed, no rotation

joint_design.type: vertical pin (part of parent) through a knuckle ring (part of child); pin is a single body of revolution grown from the bed and fused into the parent at its mushroom cap
joint_design.other_moving_surfaces: the child cavity is the exact 2D offset (r=0.5 mm) of the pin profile, so bead/groove, countersink/cap and cap rim all have a 0.5 mm normal gap (0.71 mm vertical on 45 deg flanks); socket wall to knuckle 0.5 mm; arm-to-socket faces 5.5 mm at neutral
joint_design.self_supporting: every surface inside the joint gaps is vertical or a 45 deg cone; both parts start on the bed, so no support is needed in or under any joint gap

checks.name: mesh validity
checks.result: all 4 parts watertight/manifold, 1 shell each; model.stl volume equals sum of parts (26510.6 mm3), 4 shells

checks.name: overhang analysis
checks.method: faces with downward normal flatter than 45 deg (above bed) and isolated local-minimum vertices
checks.result: none in any part (0.00 mm2), no floating islands

checks.name: neutral interference
checks.method: manifold3d boolean intersection of all part pairs

checks.name: single joint sweep
checks.method: rotate child subtree about each joint axis in 1 deg steps until first boolean intersection; clearance measured at +-20/+-30 deg

checks.name: combined poses
checks.method: all 27 combinations of (-30, 0, +30) deg on J1..J3, pairwise intersection of all 4 parts

checks.name: axial / radial retention
checks.method: translate each child continuously (0.05 mm steps) relative to its parent along +-Z, +-X, +-Y until first contact
checks.interpretation: child is captured: it can move only by the clearance (0.75 mm along Z = 0.5*sqrt2 on 45 deg flanks, 0.55 mm radially) before pin bead/cap block it; separation would need the 0.7 mm bead overlap to be forced past the lip

checks.name: slicing (no supports)
checks.result: slices without error, 280 layers, ~12.3 cm3 filament, ~1h48m

checks.name: slicing (auto supports)
checks.result: support generated only under the body belly arches (model X 59-76 mm, Z<=16.4 mm), >=13 mm from the nearest joint axis and outside every joint gap; nothing in/near the tail joints

checks.name: G-code fusion check
checks.method: per layer: extrusion tracks buffered to 0.45 mm width, matched to mesh sections of each part; flag any track region touching two parts in-layer, or one part printed on top of another part in the previous layer

limitations: All 3 joints are real, separately meshed rotating parts; no joint is faked. Motion/retention was verified geometrically and on sliced G-code only, not by a physical print.
Rotation is limited by the arm-to-socket hard stop at about +-39..41 deg; the declared working range is +-30 deg (requirement +-20 deg).
Axial retention relies on a 0.7 mm radial bead overlap; a strong pull could snap the knuckle off the bead (PLA). Not a load-bearing joint.

The 0.5 mm gaps assume a calibrated printer; strong elephant-foot on the first layer could tack the knuckle rings, pins and socket walls (all start on the bed) - enable elephant-foot compensation or break the joints loose gently after printing.
The tail lies flat on the bed (required so every joint starts on the bed and needs no support); it cannot be raised/lowered, only swung in the XY plane.

PrusaSlicer auto-support flags the pointed-arch apex under the belly (two 45 deg cones meeting); the model is designed for the no-support profile, where that apex prints as a self-supporting gothic arch. If supports are enabled anyway they stay under the belly, away from the joints.

The 100x50x60 mm limit is checked for the neutral, as-printed pose (94.99 x 26.2 x 55.99 mm). Swung to all +30 deg the width is 49.6 mm; beyond about +-30 deg on all joints together it would exceed 50 mm in Y.
Mesh-based clearance numbers are vertex-to-surface approximations (faceting $fn=96 on joint surfaces).
